1ijkow8.title: Авторы Path of Exile 2 представили новый класс Тень, лигу Завоеватели Рэкласта и обновление для PoE
1ijkow8.content:
Grinding Gear Games, как и обещала, представила дополнительные новинки релизной версии Path of Exile 2.
Ещё один новый класс — Тень
Использует кинжалы, ловушки и обман, чтобы сразить своих противников. Тень привносит с собой скрытность — новую механику, которая позволяет окутать себя темнотой и выполнить смертоносный рывок к своей цели.
«Потомок рода Перандусов, Тень однажды положился на богатство своего отца, чтобы спасти собственную жизнь. Теперь у него долг перед тёмным богом Просперо, чьё покровительство никогда не достаётся даром».На запуске у Тени будет два класса Восхождения:

Убийца — по контракту за раз, он выплачивает свой долг перед Просперо кровью.
Лазутчик — профессиональный вор, похитивший множество самых охраняемых секретов Рэкласта.

Новая лига — Завоеватели Рэкласта
В новой лиге испытаний игроки смогут примкнуть к Вареку и его наёмникам, чтобы покорить Рэкласт.
«Исследуйте новый высокоуровневый сюжет и предотвратите пробуждение древнего Кровавого Лорда. Спасайте новых союзников, ищите укрепления противника, размещайте войска на поле боя и ведите вашу армию к победе».Разработчики также вводят новую высокоуровневую систему в реальном времени для продвижения в Атласе. Игроки получат возможность назначать командиру отряд и путевые камни, чтобы зачищать карты и собирать награды.Path of Exile 2 выйдет из раннего доступа 11 декабря на PC, PlayStation 5 и Xbox Series и станет условно-бесплатной. Кампания игры получит 5 и 6 Акты:«Вернитесь в Ориат, разорённый бесчисленными катастрофами. Проложите себе дорогу через ожидающие ужасы и положите конец Сумеречному Ордену и Зверю раз и навсегда».А ещё GGG подробнее представила грядущее обновление для Path of Exile под названием «Ковены Умбрии». Оно выйдет 13 ноября на PC, PlayStation и Xbox и предложит игрокам:

новую лигу испытаний, которая столкнёт с нечестивыми ковенитами, проводящими отвратительные ритуалы ради погружения мира в бесконечную тьму;
новую систему — нити сотворения (на смену скарабеям), которая добавляет выбранную механику лиги в область, одновременно повышая редкость и сложность монстров;
переработанное древо пассивных умений Атласа;
улучшения существующих высокоуровневых систем;
новые уникальные предметы и многое другое.

3vwmt6.title: Former Nintendo of America president Doug Bowser talks about being annoyed when Switch 1 wasn’t included in console wars conversations
3vwmt6.content: Doug Bowser, the previous president of Nintendo of America, has spoken about the console wars and how it would annoy him when the original Nintendo Switch wasn’t a part of the conversation.Nintendo Switch is one of the most successful consoles of all time. Only the PlayStation 2 has sold more – and not by much.Given how well Nintendo Switch was doing and how popular it was, Bowser recently said that he’d get annoyed when the system wasn’t brought up in certain conversations involving console wars. Instead, it was sometimes only about the PlayStation and Xbox.Bowser told GamesBeat during a panel:“It’s interesting. It’s funny. I’m a pretty competitive guy. There are times when I would read news reports talking about the console wars, and they’d only mention Sony and Microsoft. WTF? We’re selling 150 million units and we’re not even included in the conversation? But there are times like this where I’m glad we’re not included in the conversation. Nintendo really chose to play in its own ocean and not get dragged down by that.”During the same talk, Bowser touched on the pre-launch jitters for Nintendo Switch as he wasn’t quite sure how consumers would react:“I was lucky that most of my tenure in my last role, it was the Nintendo Switch era. For me, it was – starting with the very first moment I saw Switch and got my hands on it, just the excitement I had over something I thought was incredibly revolutionary. Obviously Nintendo has a history in both the handheld space and the console space, but to see both of those platforms come together in one, and understanding that then we could take all of our dev talent, all of our dev capability on the game side and put it into one device – for me, I just thought that was amazing. Things were going to be heading in the right direction.But there was the unknown. How was the consumer going to react? Everyone was talking about teraflops. At the time we weren’t quite talking about raytracing, but it came shortly after. This device didn’t have some of those capabilities. I was concerned as to how consumers would react. But this all came to life for me when we had our first launch event. We were unveiling in January. People got to play the games. I always said, it’s less about what’s under the hood and more about what’s on the screen. What’s the feeling you get when you see a game, get your hands on a controller, and experience the game firsthand? That’s what makes the difference.I saw that come to life then, and of course I saw it come to life with the launch itself. Standing in front of our New York store and seeing consumers literally around the block and down past Rockefeller Center and beyond, lining up to get a Switch. And then seeing literal tears in their eyes as they came through the door, their sheer excitement and fandom for what we were about to do. That’s a pretty special moment. It’s one you don’t get to live very often.”Along with everything above, Bowser revealed today that he initially said “hell no” to taking the job at Nintendo.

9kemgt.title: Real-time strategy game The Fertile Crescent 2 is an isometric odyssey inspired by Age of Empires, with the 1.0 release out now
9kemgt.content:
Time to power-rank the biggest Bronze Age civs

Image credit: MicroProse / Rock Paper Shotgun

Age of Empires-influenced real-time strategy game The Fertile Crescent 2: Collapse of the Bronze Age leaves early access today, publishers MicroProse have announced, with the 1.0 version adding the final chapters of the singleplayer story. You'll also get your grubby fingers on the very same map editor developers Wield Interactive used to design the campaign.
I'm new to The Fertile Crescent 2 myself. I do like the sound of a strategy sim in which you guide a fugitive community through the Late Bronze Age Collapse. The land has been thrown into turmoil by the arrival of the Sea People, this being a loose historical term for assorted ocean-going migrants who, I gather, are often blamed for the crumbling of the Hittites among other once-glorious Bronze Age powers. I don't have much scholarly insight to share - I thought the "Sea People" referred to expansionist mermaids, at first - but I do have a trailer.

Watch on YouTube

Nate Crowley (RPS in peace) was exceedingly fond of the original game, calling it "a bite-sized chunk of phenomenal RTS design" that "manages to riff nostalgically on Age Of Empires, while completely rewriting its ground rules". The sequel continues with the same core concepts – above all, the paramount importance of food, which determines population and army size together with your civ's progression."This is not a game about building the biggest empire," the developers explain in a press release. "Resources have to be managed, stability is fragile, and growth comes with risk. Every expansion, every battle, and every decision must be weighed against survival. Building and managing a sustainable economy is as important as commanding your forces in battle. Expanding your army too quickly can put your food economy under pressure."
The story spans 17 missions, with four playable factions: the Assyrians, Egyptians, Babylonians, and Hittites. The 1.0 release also includes some standalone scenario missions, a skirmish mode, and multiplayer on dedicated servers with bot support.
Read more on Steam. If you're partial to historical strategy and don't mind winding back the clock (upturning the hourglass? Adjusting the sundial? Recalibrating the henge?) another few thousand years, Folk Emerging is pretty terrific. If you like stories about migrant tribes, and you don't mind trading your Hittites for Vikings, you might get a kick out of The Banner Saga.

ew9h8d.title: Terrific fantasy RPG Queen's Domain gets first proper update, adding a new throwing weapon and options to make puzzles "less frustrating"
ew9h8d.content:
Don't give up, skeleton

Image credit: Future Friends Games

Extremely good King's Field-style RPG Queen's Domain – or is it a Metroid Prime homage? Or a stealth Morrowind-up? We hacks simply cannot decide – has received its first proper patch, adding a hitherto "missing" throwing weapon, the Grave Knife, alongside a bunch of quality-of-life fixes.
They've stirred in the ability to disable screenshake, alongside some new icons to make status effects more obvious. They've also introduced "options to make some late game puzzles less frustrating", though they don't specify which. How frustrating! Still, it's a tidy overhaul for a game that has rapidly become one of my 2026 favourites.
The big mystery with the update is what the new Grave Knife does. You'll find it inside the Tower of Knowledge, once you've managed to unlock passage. As for those overly aggravating late game puzzles – I find the toughest part of puzzling in Queen's Domain is often just spotting switches and key objects, so perhaps it's something to do with that?
True, there's a large selection of skeleton tableaus who comically point the way to your next objectives, but the game's pixel aesthetics can be rather dense. I very much approve of this on the whole. I like how organic and tumbledown the environment feels - the repeated delight of realising that, yes, you can get over there, and wow, there's a whole other level down here.Queen's Domain has earned a lot of happy reactions, and is a solid commercial hit. Developers Freshly Baked say it has sold over 100,000 copies, with Vertical Slice reporting that they've already broken even. Glad tidings indeed. Find the full patch notes below, via Steam.

Fixed certain weapons counting towards Extensive Armaments challenge that were not supposed to.
Added missing throwing weapon type: Grave Knife. Available in the open chest near the middle of the Tower of Knowledge. Fixed Ring of Wind counting towards Versatile Volley challenge when it was not supposed to.
Made secret door that concealed the Pandora Blade count towards Concealed Passages challenge and added a hint for finding it.
Added options to make some late game puzzles less frustrating.
Updated status effects guide with icons to make it easier to understand which status is which visually.
Several graphical, audio, collision, and general bug fixes.
Fix getting stuck behind statue at queen's grave.
Fix soft lock from resting multiple times in a row with specific timing.
Fixed return point from falling into water on several moving objects.
Fixed bug where Steam Cloud saves didn't restore properly when switching devices after a crash.
Updated controls when scrolling a list using digital inputs: left/right inputs now scroll a full page at a time.
Added option to disable screenshake.
Fix for Herald of Okbujo death animation that made very difficult to talk to them after the fight.
Fix for talking to shopkeeper behind counter dialog getting stuck.
Fixed Dagoom the Sea King poison ring remaining forever

i80d8k.title: I just found out you can use your Steam Wishlist to search for deals on games outside of Steam, saving my nephew more than £40 on Total War: Warhammer 3
i80d8k.content:
It earned me a bucketload of uncle points

Image credit: Sega / Creative Assembly

I may be very late to the party with this discovery, but I only just realised you can connect your Steam Wishlist to a third-party deals tracker. The beauty of which is that, once hooked up, you can see what games you've been pining for are going cheap not just on Steam but through any major shopfront across the internet.
I worry that I will be coming across as 'Use this one trick to save money – greengrocers hate it!', but it's already helped save my nephew more than £40. Even if it meant using a slightly underhand method.

Two weeks ago, I got a text from my nephew asking what the best way to play Total War: Warhammer 3. When I messaged back a couple of hours later (look, I'm not a responsive uncle) to tell him it's currently £50 on Steam, but it's worth waiting because according to SteamDB's price history it's come down to £7.50 in the past, I was too late. He'd got itchy feet and bought it at full whack on Steam, using up all his birthday money.
That's when I went looking and found Is There Any Deal for the first time. (A lot of you in the comments may be throwing your hands up in despair to hear this oversight) If you've not come across it before, it's a site that tracks game sales across loads of shops, including Steam, EA Store, Epic Games Store, GamersGate, GOG. GreenManGaming, Humble. This means while a game may not be on sale on Steam you can see if it's on sale anywhere else.In the case of Total War: Warhammer 3, while it was full price on Steam, over on the Humble Store it was discounted to £7.49. I sent a link to my nephew and then told him, using the authority only an uncle has, that it's okay to refund the game through Steam and buy the cheaper version. It's not something I've ever done myself, but he's 17 and that is a lot of money to save.
Anyway, that's recommendation the first. It was only when I was looking for a way to export my Steam Wishlist to ask RPS supporters what I should cull that I realised Is There Any Deal has another feature: you can import every game on your Wishlist to get deal notifications. (This may get a second groan of despair in the comment section.) Once linked up, the site will ping you a notification whenever games you're waiting for pop up in a deal.
Just looking at my current list, I can get Genesis Noir, Ancient Enemy, and Norco for £10 total, all of which with more than 70% discounts through stores other than Steam. So, as you can see, this could be both a saving technically and lead me to spending a lot more money than I mean to…
You may already have heard of these tools, but as I hadn't I thought it best to give them a shout out.
Now considering I've revealed myself to be a rube, what other third party tools should I be installing to weaponise my Steam Library?

1nqrqqk.title: Airframe Ultra's PS1 cyberpunk city is an amazing tribute to G-Police and WipEout, and I wish you people would slow down to appreciate it
1nqrqqk.content:
But what if we could gawk at the dumpsters

Image credit: Akupara / Rock Paper Shotgun

I do not wish to "rule the streets" of Megacity West, dear creators of Airframe Ultra. I wish to be ravished by them, rubbing my face against the rusty corrugated metal of the shipping containers, and savouring the acid blue waters of the bay. I do not want to "become the one thing with freedom in a city of billions: A racer." I want to become the other thing with freedom in a city of billions: a person who slowly drives or – whisper it - walks around just looking at stuff, because gadzooks, this is one of the prettiest PS1 cyberpunk burgs I've laid eyes on.

Those eroded pastel chevrons. Those seductively wobbling vertices. That electric reef of a downtown backdrop, murderously luring your gaze from the on-coming trucks. That layer of invigorating crackle over everything. Every moment or so, I dismount from my hoverbike to inspect some concrete ruin I could swear I last saw in G-Police, or ponder the resemblance between a subway tunnel and WipEout 2097's Gare d'Europa. Then, somebody waps me in the skull with a stop sign at 300 kilometres an hour. But I was already stopped, frantic stranger! Your brutal poetic ironies are wasted on me.

Watch on YouTube

Despite my best efforts, Airframe Ultra is a battle racer. It's co-developed by Videocult, the people behind Rain World – a game it looks nothing like, but is comparable to in the sense that there is an ocean of industrial refuse to navigate, and you will very often die. Each battle race is broken into sprints around a branching course that has been smashed together by the forces of urban decay. You will corkscrew down storm drains and barge through old abandoned clifftop mansions under a scarlet sun, zip along deadly flyovers and thread the barely legible layouts of high density slums.

Your hoverbike handles like a bronco full of helium, and that's before you start wanging it off the gloriously marbled, low-poly rubbish heaps that stud the city, shunting the game's camera through surfaces and exposing the map's underside in what the absolute squares amongst my readers will doubtless deem "an inelegance", but which true turbojunkeys will appreciate for its makeshift exuberance.

You've got a boost button which generally gets you exploded – and all that's before you get to the time-limited battle arenas that bookend each sprint. Here, players attempt to slaughter each other as much as possible, spending collectible cash on floating weapon pick-ups that range from bent pipes to Gatling guns and EMP grenades. Then it's off for another sprint. The first player to earn 10 points and place first in a subsequent sprint wins the match. I have not won many matches. My primary goal right now in Airframe Ultra is persuading everybody to stop and swap some emotes, while I coo over an amazing piece of graffiti I've found.

My efforts to make Airframe Ultra a walking sim aren't just about scenery. The game is surprisingly engrossing on foot, with some woozy tank controls that make me think of the experimental days before every third-person control scheme became a variation on Assassin's Creed, Uncharted or Gears of War. You have to hammer a button to run, for instance, and you'll wind yourself fast. You can also perform punches and kicks in four directions, with grander attacks to discover by smooshing together inputs. You'd best believe I burst into tears when I realised what this reminded me of: it's Bungie's Oni! The game with the finest martial arts system ever coded! There are more obvious influences, like Road Rash, but in these grim days of endless parrying, I'll take all the Konoko callbacks I can get.

Ahhhhh. But if only this had a proper single player mode. Online and local splitscreen with drop-in bot support are all you get. I wouldn't say Airframe is the most balanced deathracer, either. In my experience, and do bear in mind I mostly try to avoid the racing component, victory typically goes to whoever lands a fat cash reserve and grabs an AK47. That mild shambolicness is arguably part of the charm, in that it supplies incentive to stop and drink in the atmosphere. These streets are big and broken and beautiful enough for all of us, friends. Let us rule them together. Read more on Steam.

udsajr.title: BioWare are gone, but at least you'll be able to watch their final days in a documentary next year and oh wait that's really sad actually
udsajr.content:
At least it's got a nice punny title

Image credit: Fennessey Films/Score G Productions

It feels like every single week for the past few years has been the infinitely quotable 30 Rock quote on repeat. That feeling struck particularly last month when EA decided to shut down the iconic Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer BioWare. That obviously resulted in the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, of which a leaked trailer and some, now former, devs made sound pretty interesting. But hey! At least there's a documentary coming next year all about the studio that managed to capture the studio's last days! Yeah, I'm not so convinced by this upside either.

As reported by Deadline, Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie will be helming a documentary about the beloved RPG studio for Canada's Super Channel. It's called, punnily enough, Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, and will apparently take a look at its origins in 1995 all the way up to its closure and a bit beyond, planned for release in 2027. Filming began two years ago, so clearly this was meant to be much more of a celebratory project than the funeral procession it's going to be.

Some big names from BioWare's history will be appearing in the doc, including its founders Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk and Augustine Yip, alongside the likes of longtime devs like Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Trent Oster, James Ohlen and Caroline Livingstone. You can also expect appearances from Jennifer Hale, Casey Hudson and, as if his sole goal is to haunt this industry everywhere, Geoff Keighley.

In a statement, co-founders Muzyka and Zeschuk said, "When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and deeply moved. BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about the stories brought to life by the amazing people on our dev teams, and the fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We’re proud this film honors those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again."

Obviously the documentary won't only be about the studio's closure, it sounds like a much bigger effort than that, so hopefully it will be a way to recognise how much of an influence BioWare has had on RPGs. It's just a ridiculous shame that it's something of a posthumous release. Continued solidarity with all those at BioWare.

ee6xqj.title: Zelda Producer Eiji Aonuma Talks About The Benefits Of "Long-Term-Tenured Staff" At Nintendo
ee6xqj.content:
"It contributes to some of the sense of continuity"
by Liam Doolan3 hours ago

Image: Nintendo Life / NintendoOne morsel from Nintendo's latest Ask the Developer interview revealed how the team behind the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake got the artist "who had created illustrations for the N64 version" to draw a new map for the Switch 2 release.
It's not every day developers reviving older games can directly consult original team members, but this is just one of many examples at Nintendo. Zelda producer, Eiji Aonuma, has now elaborated on the benefits of Nintendo's "long-term tenured staff members", explaining how it provides "balance" and the "sense of continuity" when crafting projects like the remake.Subscribe to Nintendo Life on YouTube855k

Here's what he had to say during a chat with GameSpot:

Eiji Aonuma: "I think you see a real benefit to having some very long-term-tenured staff members around who have shared the same experiences over time because every time you get to the next step, it’s easier to discuss how to proceed, or if you’re going to do something new. When you have new staff coming in, of course you want to make sure that you’re bringing everyone up with a lot of discussion, explaining how to do things, why you’re doing things certain ways, as well as the language that you’re using, but that takes some more time as well. So you need a bit of a balance. You don’t want your new staff doing things by rote or without understanding the reasons, you have to invest there. And so you do see the Zelda team change over time, but there is a continuity of core staff, certainly at least from one project to the next, so that we have that base that we can build from and bring up new staff within it. And this is something that I think Nintendo has done for a very long time, even since Miyamoto originally worked on projects like this. And it contributes to some of the sense of continuity that you do feel in games in the Zelda franchise, for example."

As the source notes, Nintendo's "unique culture" of retaining employees "for years" is often quite the contrast to local companies and studios that arguably don't show long-serving employees enough respect, and may not always consider their extensive experience and history as a positive influence moving forward.
In some cases, the dismissal of veteran staff at certain game companies has resulted in younger and less experienced teams navigating the development of remakes, remasters and sequels without any assistance or advice, as there are no long-term staff members left at the company to consult (or direct contact lines). So it's great that Nintendo seems to have found the right balance.

What do you think about Nintendo's culture and its approach to game development nowadays? Do you think the company's veteran team members and long-term employees have done a good job guiding and teaching new staff so far? Are you excited to see what its younger talent brings to the table in the future? Let us know in the comments.
[source gamespot.com]

Liam is a news writer and reviewer on Nintendo Life. He's been writing about games for more than 15 years and is a lifelong fan of many iconic video game characters. Author Profile Bluesky Reply

kud20e.title: Systemic Approach to Memory, Knowledge, and Context in Agentic AI Architectures
kud20e.content:
Key Takeaways

Context engineering beats prompt engineering - the system that builds context matters more than the prompt itself.
Separate context, memory, and knowledge -  each serves a different purpose and should be managed independently.
Balance history with real-time data - great agents combine experience with live signals.
Hallucinations are often context failures - better context leads to more reliable reasoning.
Optimize context, don't maximize it - small, relevant context outperforms large, noisy prompts.

This article is part of the "Agentic AI Architecture" article series. In this series, we try to establish agentic AI architecture as a new type of software architecture that will likely dominate the industry for years to come. The articles, written by industry experts, cover various elements and aspects of agentic AI architecture. We aim to present the latest trends and developments shaping the new type of architecture as it enters the mainstream.

As the industry moves from chatbots to autonomous agents, the architectural bottleneck is shifting. The hard problem is no longer simply retrieving data. It is deciding what an agent should know, when it should know it, how long it should remember it, and what should be forgotten. As with humans, it is one thing to know and another to remember. Hence, memory and knowledge. Knowing when to use any of the existing "knows" by bringing it to memory depends on the task context. For example, if I want to cook an omelet, I don’t necessarily need to remember how to knead dough right now. 

Let’s break it down. 

Related Sponsors

AI Security Playbook: Move Faster with AI, Without Compromising Security

Agents must reason across tools, sessions, users, and live systems, given that in an engineered system we can describe the context as a control plane. Context as a control plane is an architectural paradigm in which organizational, behavioral, and situational data (the who, what, and why) serve as the centralized governing layer for system operations, rather than being hardcoded directly into individual applications, AI models, or microservices. In our world, this will determine whether an agent acts like a reliable software system. Providing the wrong context highly increases the likelihood of the model hallucinating.

Knowledge of the system is our policies, governance, and hard truth. Knowledge acts as the system’s official textbook. It holds core business logic, strict policies, and databases. Back to our omelet example, part of the knowledge would be the need for eggs and a pan.

Memory is the critical layer that bridges historical data and real-time signals into a reasoning-ready state. What needs to be remembered for the current task? This is usually information given from knowledge, historical data, and current live events.

To summarize our three components:

Context - the immediate, active, and temporary information the agent is utilizing at any given moment. It sits directly within the model's active context window (analogous to computer RAM).
Memory - provides persistence. It allows the agent to retain information beyond a single interaction, enabling it to learn from past experiences and adapt to users over time.
Knowledge - the underlying foundation of facts, concepts, and rules that the agent inherently possesses before interacting with the user. It is the domain-specific data used to train or fine-tune the system, or the reference library to which it is granted access. Highly curated data.

Our goal in agentic systems is, when given the task context, system knowledge, and memory, to turn data into the right memory state at the right moment.

Beyond that, there are limitations to this dynamic architecture paradigm; hence, we need to systematically address the economic costs of large language model (LLM) limitations and the technical, architectural roots of hallucinations. As developers and architects, learning to avoid the common "culprits" of agentic systems mismanagement is crucial. Dive in to learn how to design a sophisticated, multi-tiered architecture for the next generation of reliable agentic AI.

Shift into Context Engine

An LLM is only as good as how we use it. While the model generates, our system determines what it sees. To avoid hallucinations, we need a trustworthy system around it. Leveraging context, knowledge, and memory. To architect the system, we will separate the model from the surrounding machinery. Going forward, for the machinery around it, we will call it a context engine. The context engine is part of the context control plane. This is the orchestrator responsible for selecting, filtering, ranking, structuring, compressing, safeguarding, and delivering information before it ever hits the LLM inference endpoint. It pulls information from knowledge, categorizes it in memory, and determines what the agent's context should be at any given millisecond. This is a meaningful shift from simple prompt engineering to systems engineering.

From Prompts to State/Context Systems

Prompt engineering assumes the task is to craft a better instruction. Context engineering assumes the real task is to build a dynamic substrate that continuously assembles the right state for reasoning. The prompt is no longer about "What should I ask the model?" It is "What is the minimal, highest-value context the model needs in order to reason well right now?"

In a production-grade agentic architecture, we require dynamic systems that dictate what an agent "knows" at any given millisecond. Our system goal is to take what’s relevant and compile a new prompt encompassing the required information to improve the model's success likelihood.

Context as a Compiler

To understand how the Context Engine behaves, consider the analogy of a modern software compiler. A compiler translates high-level source code into machine-executable instructions; the context engine translates vast oceans of unstructured, disconnected raw, real-time, and historical data into a structured, reasoning-ready state. It builds a deterministic state machine that allows the probabilistic agent to execute safely. It ensures that inputs are authenticated, validated against business logic, stripped of personally identifiable information (PII), and securely sandboxed before the LLM generates a plan of action.

Thinking Through Architecture

Effective software architecture for autonomous AI agents requires reconciling several fundamentally conflicting paradigms of data management and data flow.

Historical vs. Real-Time Memory Streams

A robust agentic architecture must gracefully balance long-term "episodic" memory with immediate "sensory" input. Meaning that to build a useful context engine, our architecture must reconcile two very different categories of state: historical memory and real-time input.

Historical memory is the long-lived layer. It includes prior interactions, past decisions, user preferences, domain rules, internal documentation, and accumulated observations. This is what gives an agent continuity. It allows the system to behave as though it has experience.

Real-time input is the short-lived layer. It includes the current task, the latest events, live telemetry, fresh tool outputs, and environmental changes. This is what keeps the agent grounded in the present.

While vector databases excel at retrieving historical, semantic facts, agentic workflows frequently pivot on sub-second, real-time context. For example, if an AI DevOps agent is triaging a server outage, retrieving an architectural runbook from a vector store (episodic memory) is only half the battle. The agent also needs the live error log stream from the last five seconds (sensory memory). The architecture must fuse these batch and streaming sources asynchronously, ensuring the agent acts on a unified, up-to-date reality. 

This architecture must have balance. If it over-indexes on history/episodic memory, the agent becomes stale. It will keep replaying yesterday’s assumptions into today’s reality. If it over-indexes on real-time data, the agent becomes reactive and forgetful. It may respond to the latest signal but fail to incorporate the broader context that gives that signal meaning.

Luckily for us, this tension is not new. Distributed systems have always had to reconcile durable state with transient events. Agent systems inherit the same problem, but with an additional challenge: the reasoning layer is probabilistic, expensive, and bounded by a limited context window. This adds an important layer of constraint optimization to the context architecture design - deciding which information to keep, which can be compressed, which must be revalidated, and which should be excluded entirely. The goal is not just freshness or completeness. The goal is usefulness under constraint.

Figure 1: Historical Data vs Real-Time Memory Streams (Source: created by the author with Gemini)

Knowledge vs. Raw Data (SELECT * vs. Cumulative Insight)

One of the most common architectural mistakes in AI systems is treating retrieval as if it were enough, ie, operating under the semantic equivalent of a SQL SELECT *, assuming more information must be better. Architectures that attempt to consistently retrieve large volumes of data will inevitably fail at scale. We can think of retrieval as how we get data into the system, yet it does not guarantee that the data is useful, timely, coherent, or appropriately ranked for the decision at hand. This is what standard RAG pipelines are all about. They are often built to retrieve raw, fragmented, and overlapping data chunks. In actuality, using this approach would most likely result in the system dumping 10 unedited wiki pages into a prompt, making the LLM waste compute cycles trying to sort the noise from the signal - yet failing due to relevant signals buried under less important and more noisy ones. Hence, the right information and shape of the data, which we refer to as knowledge, matter more than raw data.

True Knowledge Curation focuses on cumulative insight. Instead of injecting raw data, the architecture employs background workers/ML pipelines that distill, aggregate, and rank retrieved data by relevance, using the up-to-date system state. To achieve that, we need to build dedicated pipelines that transform raw data into structured knowledge graphs or condensed summaries. For example, taking a large database and creating a pipeline that summarizes a million data entries into one entry every 12 hours. This way, we ensure the model receives a small, synthesized body of knowledge (1 entry point in the database) rather than a chaotic stream of consciousness (the whole database, sometimes).

Custom Context: The End of "One-Size-Fits-All"

Foundational models like GPT-4 and Claude, as well as vector databases like Pinecone and Milvus, have become an accessible commodity. Everyone can access them today through their services. Yet, this is not the same for context; the architectural principles for working with context are highly domain-specific. Every company should design its own context based on the business domain and the product it serves. For example, a fintech firm might choose to curate context for an autonomous fraud-analysis agent by prioritizing transaction timestamps, geolocation anomalies, and strict compliance rules. This will look entirely different for a legal tech firm. A legal tech firm might choose to curate context based on state law for use with an agent that generates contracts. We are learning that the context itself cannot be generic; it must reflect the unique domain logic, security boundaries, and vocabulary of the specific product.

The Context Lifecycle: Managing Knowledge & Hallucination at Scale

Treating context as a continuous lifecycle allows us, as engineering teams, to manage knowledge systematically and directly address the root causes of model failure and prohibitive inference costs.
The Lifecycle Stages

Generally speaking, there are 4 stages: Selection, Injection, Compression, Expiration & Refresh.  Figure 2 describes how each stage could be a dedicated module in our architecture or a standalone service.

Figure 2: Agentic AI Systemic Context Lifecycle (Source: created by the author with Gemini)

Selection (Retrieval & Filtering)

The first and most important step. This is where the system identifies which data points are likely to matter for the current task. The system's goal is to identify the absolute highest-value data points across multiple data stores. Advanced architectures have moved beyond simple cosine similarity in vector spaces, implementing hybrid search algorithms that combine dense semantic search with sparse keyword search (e.g., BM25) and knowledge graph traversal to ensure precision. In this process, we want to understand intent, task type, risk, user role, and temporal relevance. It is important to remember that the same underlying corpus may yield different contexts for a troubleshooting agent, a research agent, and a support summarization agent. This is where architecture begins to diverge from product. As part of the design requirements, we need to identify and define what is risky and what is actionable.

Injection

Once the system knows what matters, it has to place that information into the model’s working context (aka context window) in a useful form. While the end result might look like simple string concatenation, the path to getting there requires more deliberate design. That design involves semantic templating, ensuring the data is formatted to match the user's explicit intent, including necessary system instructions, few-shot examples, and output schema constraints (such as JSON definitions). To understand the importance of this step, consider how it affects the entire system. In our world, this placement of information changes how models reason. Hence, order, grouping, and structured state matter. 

Compression (Summarization & Distillation)

Processing a large context is expensive. To respect token limits, historical data should be iteratively compressed. Utilizing smaller, faster LLMs (or even deterministic algorithms) to summarize conversation histories or condense long documents saves massive amounts of space and reduces latency for the primary reasoning model. Test summaries carefully to avoid distortions. There are statistical models available today to assess summary validity, such as the Perplexity (PPL) Ratio, Token-Level Kullback-Leibler (KL) Divergence, the Chi-Square Test for Categorical Outputs, and others.

Expiration and Refresh

Context that never expires eventually turns into a liability. Agents need mechanisms to retire stale assumptions, refresh live facts, and separate durable truths from temporary observations. A system preference might remain stable across months or change overnight. A product configuration might change in minutes. A support incident may be relevant for a day and misleading a week later. Without expiration and refresh, systems fall into stale data loops: they keep reusing context that was once correct but is now simply persuasive. Hence, constantly testing and validating the system through feedback loops is a must. This should be tailored to the system's end goal. For example, in a car-sharing system, the goal is to satisfy users; hence, if user satisfaction drops suddenly, it’s best to explore underlying factors that may need refreshing. 

Hallucination Is Often a Context Failure

LLM hallucinations are rarely the result of a "broken" model; they are almost always the symptom of an unmanaged, impoverished context window. Because LLMs are probabilistic, when an agent lacks the explicit, factual data required to answer a prompt or execute a task, its underlying mechanism forces it to "guess" based on latent training weights.

Proactive context management acts as a strict guardrail. By saturating the model with highly relevant, high-confidence knowledge and explicitly instructing it to reason only based on the provided context, we can effectively suppress latent, inaccurate associations. In a productionized agentic system, a well-engineered context engine becomes our primary defense against hallucinated actions.

Token Economics: The Cost-to-Performance Trade-off

Processing a large context is notoriously expensive. Every token injected into the prompt window incurs both a computational latency cost and a strict financial cost. Token Economics is the engineering discipline of optimizing "attention real estate" within the LLM's limitations.

The recent expansion of context windows (e.g., models boasting 128k to 1M+ token limits) has tempted developers towards lazy architecture. They dump entire code repositories or massive troves of documents into the prompt. This drastically increases Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) latency, skyrockets API billing costs, and, ironically, degrades model performance. The model suffers from the "Lost in the Middle" phenomenon, shown in Figure 3. This problem was identified by Stanford researchers Nelson F. Liu et al. in 2023, where the model fails to retrieve facts buried in the center of massive context windows and only focuses on edge case information. The larger the bottom part of the U shape (context window), the less accurate the response will be. This research explains why we want the context sent to the model to be relatively small. This approach makes the U bottom part smaller as well - hence, improving outcomes. 

Architects must weigh the marginal utility of every retrieved document against its token cost and relevancy. Just because we can send 100,000 tokens doesn't mean we should. Strict context budgeting, iterative pruning, and caching mechanisms are mandatory for scalable economics.

Figure 3: Lost in the middle problem - recall vs accuracy (Source: created by the author with Gemini - based on Lost in the Middle scientific paper by Stanford)

Designing Tiered Memory Architectures

Designing systemic approaches to memory requires establishing firm boundaries for how agents retain, update, or discard knowledge across sessions. Drawing inspiration from human cognitive architecture, systems should be multi-tiered:

Working Memory (The Prompt Window): The immediate, ephemeral state required to execute the current step in a workflow. It is highly constrained and resets per inference call.
Short-term Memory (Session Cache): Often managed via in-memory data stores like Redis. This tracks the current conversational state, intermediate steps of an ongoing task, and recent actions over the last few minutes or hours.
Long-term Memory (Asynchronous Persistence): The permanent storage of synthesized insights, user preferences, and historical facts. This relies on vector databases and knowledge graphs, which are updated asynchronously, so that the agent's core "understanding" grows over time without bloating the real-time retrieval pipeline.

How to Mitigate Architectural Anti-Patterns

There are a few recurring failure patterns that show up again and again in agentic systems.

Architectural Anti-Pattern
Description
Systemic Impact
Mitigation

Context Stuffing
Injecting every plausible document, log, and tool result into the prompt under the assumption that "more is better."
Creates severe noise, dilutes model attention, increases latency, and degrades precision.
Implement strict relevance scoring thresholds. If a retrieved document's semantic similarity score falls below a certain confidence interval, drop it entirely rather than stuffing it into the prompt.

Stale Data Loops
Reusing historical context (like user states or system configs) without a mechanism to validate its current accuracy.
Agents become confidently wrong, consistently acting on outdated realities.
Implement metadata filtering during retrieval that cross-references timestamps, or utilize event-driven architectures (like Kafka) to proactively invalidate stale embeddings.

Generic Retrieval
Utilizing a sta

fw63tn.title: AWS Capacity Largely Sold out through 2027, with On-Demand Headroom Reserved
fw63tn.content:
Amazon CEO Andy Jassy recently said that AWS’s large committed cloud capacity is largely sold out through 2027, with a good chunk of 2028 already allocated, while the company continues to reserve headroom for On Demand, EC2 and Bedrock.

Jassy made the remarks in a video podcast with Andreessen Horowitz co-founder Ben Horowitz and general partner Erik Torenberg, reported by Reuters on October 23. AWS sells capacity assurance through On-Demand Capacity Reservations and Capacity Blocks for ML, where a customer reserves instances in a named Availability Zone, and in the Capacity Blocks case, for a fixed window beginning on a future date. As previously reported on InfoQ, AWS raised Capacity Blocks for ML rates by about 15% uniformly across every region in January, covering P5en, P5e, P5 and P4d GPU instances along with Trn2 and Trn1.

Capacity for 2026 is already gone, Jassy said, and the company could invest well beyond the roughly $220 billion in capital expenditure planned for this year without it being a poor use of capital. On the allocation itself:

2027 is largely sold out. We always leave a certain amount for on demand and our inference service bedrock, or EC2, but largely sold out all the big chunks. A good chunk of 2028 is sold out.

Cloud analyst David Linthicum argued that the reporting overstated the position, drawing a distinction between the pre-reserved blocks Jassy described and what an enterprise can allocate day to day:

Of course, I suspect I can still go into the AWS console today and allocate GPU capacity for AI workloads. Maybe not the exact massive, pre-reserved, hyperscale capacity block some large model provider wants for the next three years, but that’s not exactly the same thing as "AWS is sold out."

Linthicum added that the market already carries enough confusion around reserved instances, on-demand services and committed capacity, and that headlines of this kind lead to bad assumptions and bad strategy.

Discussion on Reddit turned to current availability rather than the 2027 commitments. The highest-rated comment, from a developer posting as cbigsby, describes constraints on ordinary instance types:

We’ve been seeing a big rise in compute capacity issues the past month or so at work, just for regular ec2 instances. Forget spot instances we have trouble getting enough on demand. Luckily mostly tied to CI but there have been a few days where the production k8s clusters have been concerningly constrained.

Similar reports appeared elsewhere. Richard T., a technical operations manager, commented on Linthicum’s post that Microsoft has released only limited information about Azure East US capacity constraints, and that his team adopted reserved instances to secure capacity against projected growth. A commenter in a parallel thread reported trouble obtaining sufficient compute from any of the three major providers, and said the constraint was not limited to GPUs.

Ian Rae, replying to Linthicum, pointed to the architectural consequence of that response:

next thing you know, folks reserve cloud resources they are worried they might need, which is an anti-cloud pattern

AWS already ships tooling for the problem Rae describes. As reported on InfoQ last October, EC2 Capacity Manager aggregates capacity data into a cross-account, cross-region dashboard and reports the ratio of used to unused reserved capacity as a measure of reservation efficiency.

The $220 billion figure covers total capital expenditure rather than AI spending alone, a distinction raised by commenters in both threads. Amazon reports third-quarter results on October 29, where its remaining performance obligations disclosure will show how much of the committed capacity is contracted revenue.

yoiuk8.title: Avery the Poké Kid's Father Pleads With The Pokémon Company to Make a Trading Card in Honor of His Late Son
yoiuk8.content: The father of late Pokémon influencer Avery the Poké Kid is asking The Pokémon Company to create a special card in honor of his son.Avery the Poké Kid was a prominent and cheerful voice in the Pokémon Trading Card Game community. He died in September 2026 at 12 years old in after a seven-year-battle with pancreatic cancer; he went viral posthumously when his family shared a video of his final card pack opening a few days after his death, in which he excitedly pulled a 30th Anniversary Jirachi SIR card.Now, his father is putting forth a public request to The Pokémon Company to make a special card in Avery’s honor.On November 6, Christian Garcia — Avery’s father — published a tearful video on Instagram with a special plea to "immortalize" his son in the hobby he loved the most.“Trying to figure out how to carry on Avery’s legacy has been the biggest challenge of the last couple months,” Garcia said. “…I want to make a plea to anyone, literally anyone from The Pokémon Company: If you’re watching this video, I want to figure out how to immortalize him somehow in the trading card game he loved so much. “That kid literally was the embodiment of a Pokémon Master, and we’re hopeful, and I think it would be the coolest thing to open up a pack of cards and chase our son. If someone at The Pokémon Company is watching, please get a hold of us.”Fans and fellow collectors are doing everything they can to get the attention of The Pokémon Company, with most agreeing that it would only make sense to make his card some iteration of a Jirachi, given his viral pull that took over social media after his death.Avery’s heartbreaking Jirachi pull even caught the attention of the card’s artist, who posted an emotional reaction to the news on her Twitter/X account. “I’m so deeply moved. I’m so glad I kept drawing. I’ve honestly been in tears ever since I saw this,” she wrote. “‘I want my art to bring happiness to people.’ That’s one of the reasons I draw. I’m so glad I put that wish into this piece.”This latest statement from Avery’s father follows a September announcement from the influencer’s family in response to scalpers inflating the price of the 30th Anniversary Jirachi SIR card as a result of his viral video.“We are not involved in or benefiting from any cards being sold in Avery’s name or likeness. We have not approved these sales. We have asked sellers to take their listings down. Please do so immediately. This does not honor Avery’s generous heart. We are mourning our son and caring for our children. Please let us do that in peace,” they wrote at the time.Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. r5b4rj.title: GTA 6 Players in Germany Can Legally Take Time Off Work to Play the Game on Launch, But There's a Catch
r5b4rj.content: Updated: Nov 6, 2026 8:18pm UTCGermany has a unique legal loophole that lets 60 employees take time off work to play GTA 6 without putting their jobs in jeopardy.GTA 6 is shaping up to be one of the biggest pop culture moments in history, and perhaps the biggest video game launch of all time. With this in mind, it’s no surprise that oodles of gamers are planning to call out of work to play it, with estimates showing a 17% increase in time-off requests for its launch date on November 19.This trend isn’t limited to the US, either, as a fair amount of fans across the globe will also be staying home to play. Luckily, fans in Germany literally have legal protections that will allow them to do this without putting their jobs on the line.Bildungsurlaub, Germany's legally mandated paid learning leave for certified training courses, is offering a state-funded educational course on storytelling in video games that would give gamers three days off to play GTA 6 from November 18 - 20. Titled ‘Open World Games: Lessons from a Digital World,’ this program is open to 60 participants, letting them use this paid leave to “explore storytelling, digital culture, and collaboration through open-world gaming,” as explained in a press release shared with IGN.Students will gather in guided groups to complete assignments in the game and use their observations to learn “practical lessons on storytelling, motivation, community-building, and collaboration.” One of these lessons explores how Easter eggs create engagement with players, examining how brands, learning programs, and teams can “borrow from that dynamic.”“Modern learning should meet people where their curiosity already lives. Open worlds are built on stories, choices, communities, and constant problem-solving. That makes them powerful places to learn,” says Carlo Dreschel, founder of course provider Dein Bildungsurlaub. “Like many other educational providers, we've incorporated elements of gaming, such as role-playing, simulations, game mechanics and reward systems, into learning experiences before. But with ‘Open World Games,’ we're taking that approach to an entirely new level.”23-year-old accountant Victoria is one of the students who’s signed up for this course. Hailing from Berlin, she’s an “avid gamer” who says she’s curious about how this program will aid her professional life. “I am curious to see what I can really learn from the experience. My usual day to day is driven by routine. I believe the course will break this routine and offer a new perspective to the same old problems. Maybe the experience of pulling off a high speed car chase can help me handle stressful clients in the future,” she said in a statement.Participants must be 18 years of age or older and have access to a suitable device and a licensed open-world game in order to take part in this course. It will take place over a three-day period online, with an additional in-person event planned in Berlin.Germany isn't the only country getting ahead of the GTA 6 employment crater; Australia's workplace regulator put out a helpful graphic informing workers of their paid leave rights ahead of the game's launch. And in July, a flyer from the 9th Engineer Battalion in Fort Stewart, Georgia went viral for offering recruits a four-day pass to play GTA 6 with a “special reenlistment incentive." We at IGN even polled our readers to see how many of you are planning to take time off work to play the game, and the results were surprisingly split down the middle. GTA 6 launches November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox X/S.Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. 8wwg26.title: Ed Boon Wants to Know What Fans Want the Next Mortal Kombat Game to Be Called
8wwg26.content:
Updated: Nov 6, 2026 9:21pm UTCEd Boon is stirring up excitement in the fighting game community after releasing a poll asking fans what they’d like the next Mortal Kombat installment to be called.It’s been a rough time for Mortal Kombat fans. The series’ latest game, MK1, officially stopped receiving new content updates in May 2025, and its presence at competitive tournaments has been lackluster, at best.Players are eager for more news on the next game in the franchise, which co-creator Ed Boon confirmed was officially in the works in May 2026. It’s been pretty quiet since then — but now, it appears that Boon is testing the waters to see what fans are expecting.On November 6, 2026, Boon published two polls on X/Twitter. The first asked, “What would you want the next Mortal Kombat to be called?” giving options for Mortal Kombat 13, Mortal Kombat 12, and Mortal Kombat 2. (Thus far, 43% of participants have voted for Mortal Kombat 2, with 33% choosing 13 and 23% choosing 12.)His second poll is far more intriguing, asking: “With two great Marvel fighting games being made by different teams, which would you like to see come out next? Marvel Tokon 2 by Arc System Works, or Marvel vs Capcom 4?” (Unsurprisingly, the overwhelming majority of fans chose MvC4.)With 2 great Marvel fighting games being made by different teams. Which would you like to see come out next?Marvel Tokkon 2 by Arc System works.orMarvel vs Capcom 4— Ed Boon (@noobde) November 6, 2026
This is an interesting query coming from the developer of the Injustice series, and an odd one, given that the likelihood of another Marvel vs Capcom game happening anytime soon — if ever — seems extremely improbable. The FGC has already tied itself in knots about Tokon’s player count and difficult PC launch, while, mechanically, there’s a significant divide as to whether or not it’s actually fun at a competitive level. On the other hand, the MvC series appeared to die a slow, painful death with Infinite, though it has received a second wind over the last few years (in no small part thanks to the Beyond fan mod).This question follows oodles of rumors regarding the next Injustice game, which has been all but outright confirmed by Boon. Fans have already uncovered resumes from stunt performers that list Injustice 3, and rumors that playtests were underway for the game surfaced earlier this year. Boon reacted to the rumors back in September in response to a tweet claiming that NetherRealm was testing Injustice 3, Mortal Kombat 13, and / or Mortal Kombat 9. “All false,” he wrote. “Appreciate the interest & enthusiasm, but just because a game isn’t currently being tested externally doesn’t necessarily mean the game isn’t in development.”For now, we’ll just have to wait and see what Boon and NetherRealm have in store for their next game. In the meantime, you can read our interview with the cast of the Street Fighter movie, who said they’re more than willing to take part in a crossover film with the cast of the Mortal Kombat franchise. Boon even responded to our report, saying that he’d rather have a Street Fighter x Mortal Kombat game before a movie gets made.Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. nkevhw.title: God of War Ragnarok Tops List of 10 Highest-Grossing PlayStation Studios Games From the PS5 Generation
nkevhw.content:
Updated: Nov 6, 2026 7:33pm UTCSony Santa Monica Studios' God of War Ragnarok tops the list of highest-grossing PlayStation Studios games of the PS5 generation, according to Alinea Analytics.The game data company's head of market analysis, Rhys Elliott, shared information related to sales for titles published under the PlayStation banner in a Substack post today. It features a list of 10 games estimated to have emerged as Sony's best performers so far.You can probably guess at least some of the games that managed to crack the top 10 list, but there are a few interesting inclusions in there, too. God of War Ragnarok, for example, is placed at number one with an estimated $1.4 billion in gross revenue. Spider-Man 2 is second at $1.3 billion, with Gran Turismo 7 placed third at $841.9 million. You can see the full list below.Here's the 10 top-grossing PlayStation Studios games of this generation (@alineaanalytics estimates). Together, the 10 games generated over $6.5 billion across PlayStation (84.7%), Steam (14.1%), and Xbox (1.2% via just Helldivers 2).Full write-up over on Substack. https://t.co/3XLgJdTqUM— Rhys Elliott (@superhys) November 6, 2026
PlayStation Studios' Top 10 Highest-Grossing PS5 Games, According to Alinea Analytics1. God of War Ragnarok – $1.4 billion2. Spider-Man 2 – $1.3 billion3. Gran Turismo 7 – $841.9 million4. Helldivers 2 – $786.3 million5. Horizon Forbidden West – $485.8 million6. Ghost of Yōtei – $410.1 million7. The Last of Us Part 1 – $341.3 million8. Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart – $334.9 million9. Stellar Blade – $316.9 million10. Astro Bot – $292.6 millionThese 10 games alone have generated $6.5 billion for PlayStation. Although the list only includes titles from the PS5 generation, the numbers here do account for other platforms. Astro Bot, for example, is exclusive to PS5 and earned its amount only through the estimated 4.7 million copies it sold on that platform.God of War Ragnarok, meanwhile, is also available on PS4 and PC, with Alinea Analytics' breakdown showing its revenue accumulated via 21.6 million copies across all three platforms. Of its performance on PlayStation, 75.2% of its 20.1 million share of copies sold were on PS5, specifically, with 27.5% of all sales on PS4 and PS5 being physical. Elliott called the Norse God of War sequel an evergreen title for Sony, explaining that in 2026 alone it's managed to sell 1.1 million copies. That's an impressive feat compared even to brand-new games from this year, and it's only more impressive when you consider that it was made accessible to PlayStation Extra subscribers nearly two years ago in January of 2025. Alinea Analytics estimates show that 6.7 million PlayStation Plus users have accessed it via the service.Ghost of Yōtei may have technically been trailing behind its predecessor as of October, but at least for now, its recent Echoes of Sekigahara expansion has helped it land in sixth. As of today's update, it's said to have sold 5.5 million copies as a PS5 exclusive. Another interesting addition from the list is Stellar Blade, which is technically a second-party release published by PlayStation Studios. Today's data accounts for sales across PS5 and Steam (a Nintendo Switch 2 version launched yesterday) and shows that 59.7% of its revenue was earned from the former and 40.3% from the latter.Alinea Analytics' breakdown is not an official look into where sales are at with Sony's gaming division. Meanwhile, its update follows official information released by the PlayStation company just earlier this week. It came with the news that it had raised its sales forecast while also sharing figures for Marvel's Wolverine for the first time. For more, you can see how PlayStation's Bloodborne has held up in the 11 years since its launch on PS4.Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

4g8nq8.title: Blizzard Reveals What Made It Finally Pull The Trigger on WoW Forever
4g8nq8.content: Updated: Nov 6, 2026 6:47pm UTCWorld of Warcraft Forever came out earlier this week, and has been a massively successful launch. It almost begs the question, "Why wait this long?" Well, Blizzard has revealed what made it finally release the Classic+ game mode. In an interview with Bloomberg, Blizzard senior game designer Josh Greenfield revealed that the developer had been kicking around the idea of WoW Forever since before Classic released in 2019, but the team ultimately pulled the trigger on the straight-up port of Vanilla WoW first. But while Forever was put on the backburner, the Classic team started to get a little bit more experimental as the old-school version of the MMO aged. Then, in 2023, Blizzard released a new game mode, Season of Discovery, which took Classic and made some pretty radical changes, like ability gems and turning old 5-player dungeons like Blackfathom Deeps into full-scale raids. This game mode had some pretty immediate impacts on even retail WoW, like when Blizzard released Mists of Pandaria Remix in 2024 and Legion Remix in 2025. But it turns out that the biggest impact that Season of Discovery had was making the WoW team pull the trigger on Classic+, or Forever. According to Greenfield, the community response to Season of Discovery is what made Forever actually happen. He told Bloomberg, “That’s really when the conversation started around, ‘Hey, what does a permanent version of this game look like?’”Season of Discovery's success also helped convince leadership to allow development on Forever to proceed, and once the team started getting the new graphics engines in place, everything seems to come together. According to that Bloomberg piece, Northshire Abbey became a tech demo of sorts, and one that won over pretty much everyone at Blizzard. And it's good that it did. IGN's early review of World of Warcraft Forever is extremely positive, and while it'll obviously be a while before the full review is finished, reviewer Len Hafer says, "[Blizzard] made me believe I can go home again – and that home is somewhere I want to spend more time, with new surprises to discover. Let's see if they can keep it up for 47 more levels. Watch this space for updates in the weeks to come."Players seem impressed with WoW Forever as well, especially on the back of an extremely smooth launch that was almost completely free of any kind of server problems. It doesn't hurt that Blizzard dedicated a ton of hardware to keeping the servers running smoothly at launch, with around 200TB of memory. Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. ГЛАВА ПОЛЬСЬКОГО МЗС РАДОСЛАВ СІКОРСЬКИЙ. ФОТО ЗІ СТОРІНКИ МЗС ПОЛЬЩІ В Х

Реклама:

Він додав, що саме Росія має зрозуміти: її подальша агресія проти України буде пов'язана зі зростаючими витратами та наслідками.

РЕКЛАМА:

Як він зазначив, підтвердженням важливої ролі Польщі та її рішучості є військові навчання коаліції охочих, що відбудуться в листопаді. Він також підкреслив, що "Україна не повинна вести переговори щодо свого майбутнього під тиском обстрілів цивільного населення".

"Жодне рішення не може бути нав'язане Україні без її згоди та присутності за столом переговорів. Так само, як безпека Європи не може бути предметом переговорів, що ведуться без нашої участі. Головна дипломатка ЄС Кая Каллас заявила, що Європа має власні безпекові інтереси щодо завершення російсько-української війни, а тому повинна брати участь у переговорному процесі.

Нагадаємо, президент США Дональд Трамп заявив, що у четвер, 5 листопада, провів приватну зустріч із посланцем Путіна і анонсував "чудову угоду", яка стосуватиметься не лише України і Росії, а й Європи загалом.
